sample.title: Triangulation
sample.content: Triangulation is a method of determining the distance between two points by measuring angles from a known baseline and applying trigonometric relationships. It allows measurement of large or inaccessible distances without physically traversing the entire span.

sample.title: Measuring distance between mountain tops by triangulation
sample.content: It would be difficult to measure the horizontal distance between two mountain tops using only a meter stick. We have found by experience that distance can be measured in another fashion: by triangulation.

sample.title: Apply
sample.content: Apply triangulation techniques to calculate the horizontal distance between two remote points when direct measurement is impractical.

sample.title: Triangulation only measures angles, not distances
sample.content: Students often think triangulation is used only to determine angles. In reality, triangulation uses known distances and measured angles to calculate unknown distances, making it a powerful method for measuring large separations such as between mountain tops.

sample.title: Summary
sample.content: Distance can be subdivided analogously to time: a smaller unit is chosen and the number of such units required to compose a larger unit is counted, allowing progressively finer measurements. However, practical measurement of large horizontal separations, such as between mountain peaks, cannot rely solely on a meter stick. Experience shows that distance can be determined by alternative methods, notably triangulation, which uses geometric relationships to infer lengths without direct physical measurement.
